response.sql: WITH pt AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) AS d1, AVG(l.APTT - l.PT) AS d2 FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), sx AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(d1) AS a1, AVG(d2) AS a2 FROM pt GROUP BY SEX), m AS (SELECT AVG(a2) AS mean_a2 FROM sx) SELECT AVG(sx.a1) AS avg_alb_minus_tp, AVG(sx.a2) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt, AVG(sx.a2) - (SELECT mean_a2 FROM m) AS exceeds_mean_by FROM sx WHERE sx.a2 > (SELECT mean_a2 FROM m)

assumptions.assumption: Each row difference (ALB-TP, APTT-PT) is computed per lab record, so records missing either value are ignored for that difference; patient averages are then averaged per sex, unweighted by patient or record count. Sexes whose APTT-PT average is null are ignored in the mean.
The 'mean of the sex-level APTT-PT averages' is the simple average over all sexes (including NULL/blank groups), and the 'exceeds' figure is the average over the kept sexes minus that mean.
